name: Climate Resilience Grant Program (New York)
summary: Grants for New York land trusts and other conservation groups to acquire land or easements, or to fund planning and capacity work, that protect lands and waters important for climate resilience.

amount.note: Up to $50,000 for land acquisition projects; up to $25,000 for planning and capacity projects.

eligibility.rule: NY land trust, conservation 501(c)(3), nonprofit academic body, local agency, or state/federal Tribe or its nonprofit
Lands acquisition: in a mapped focal area, or nearby with exceptional conservation and engagement if funding allows
For Waters acquisition, the parcel or tract contains or intersects with shorelines or mapped hydrological features
Does not propose shoreline or streambank stabilization, including living shorelines
Submit at most one application to this programme per year
Acquisition parcels share ownership. Non-adjacent parcels have a relationship that promotes landscape connectivity.

documents: Conflict Inquiry form, if a non-profit organization
Current LTAC accreditation letter, plus renewal proof if renewing before grant end
Accreditation letter of intent submitted within the past year, if applicable to a non-accredited nonprofit
IRS determination letter for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Bylaws and articles of incorporation for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Latest Form 990 or financial statement for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Home-state Certificate of Good Standing for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits

applicant_types.quote: Funding is available to land trusts and other conservation organizations, academic institutions, Tribal Nations, municipalities and local agencies.

geography.quote: The goal of the program is to support New York's conservation community in protecting the lands and waters that contribute to New York's resilience to climate change

access.quote: Apply Now to either of the two funding categories.

window.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026. Applications close January 22, 2027.

amount.quote: Applicants may apply for up to $50,000 for Land Acquisition projects or $25,000 for Planning and Capacity projects.

pool.quote: The total amount of funding available is $650,000.

effort.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026 and are due by January 22, 2027.
Scoring Criteria All projects will be evaluated for:

eligibility.quote: The program is open to all land trusts and other non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations with a conservation-related mission, non-profit academic institutions, State or Federally Recognized Tribal Nations (as well as affiliated non-profits applying on their behalf), municipalities, and village, town and county agencies that operate in New York State.

Conserving Resilient Lands Acquisition projects will also be evaluated for: • • • Location: the project is within a mapped focal area. Projects with outstanding conservation values and compelling community engagement attributes that are outside of but close to a focal area may be considered as funding allows.

Projects in this category are not limited to the Climate Resilient Lands focal areas and may include any parcel or tract that contains or intersects with shorelines or any of the hydrological features shown in the map viewer.
All projects must be completed by June 30, 2028, which is approximately 12 months from the beginning of the grant term.
Shoreline and streambank stabilization projects, including living shorelines, are not eligible.
Applicants may submit one application per year to the CRGP.

Yes, but they must be under the same ownership and preferably adjacent to one another. If they are not adjacent, they may still constitute a single project if there is a clear conservation relationship between them that promotes landscape connectivity
Are land acquisition projects that already closed eligible? o No. This program is intended to catalyze new protection projects that need to close a funding gap.

after_award.quote: For Planning, Capacity and Strategy projects, grantees must submit brief interim and final reports.
For Land Acquisition projects, grantees must send a copy of the recorded deed to Matt Levy mlevy@tnc.org no later than 60 days from the date of closing.

documents.quote: The Conflict Inquiry form is required for all non-profit organizations.

Land trusts that are currently accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission (LTAC) and will maintain their accreditation through 2027 must upload their current accreditation letter. If you are in, or will enter a renewal period before the end of the grant term, please provide your current accreditation letter along with documentation showing that you are in the renewal process.

Letter of Intent for accreditation, submitted within the past year (if applicable) o IRS determination letter o Organizational by-laws and articles of incorporation o Most recent Form 990 or Financial Statement o Certificate of Good Standing from State where organization is located
